title: The Last Oath Anew
premise: Xanthe Voss, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, serves a guild that trades in impossible things — until the night the border wards collapse and the stars go out, erasing their country from every map and memory but their own. Guided by a disgraced cartographer who once betrayed them and a guild apprentice who may be more than human, Xanthe must find the Door of Anew, the only exit from a nation that no longer exists. But the Door demands an oath renewed in blood, and renewing it means surrendering the person they have become. In the end, Xanthe speaks a new oath entirely — one that binds them to the people beside them rather than the guild behind them — and holds the door open long enough for everyone else to pass through, choosing exile and love over duty and erasure.
about_author: Dominic Nystrom is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of countries that no longer exist. They write fantasy about borders, oaths, and the quiet violence of belonging.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A night of routine work at the Guild of Improbable Exchanges: appraising a bottled memory, balancing accounts, deflecting the flirtations of apprentice Wren Solace. Through Xanthe we see the weight of an inherited oath and a life of careful, lonely order. Emotional beat: competent isolation, the ache of a duty with no living witnesses.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The border wards fall with a sound like tearing silk; the stars vanish; the horizon simply stops. The guild master orders everyone to hold position, but Xanthe feels their oath-sword humming with wrongness. Wren refuses to stay behind. Emotional beat: dread blooming into vertigo as the familiar world becomes uncanny.

chapters.title: A Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The city outside is intact but unmoored — neighbors remember different histories, roads loop back on themselves. Wren, secretly not fully human, can still read the geography's true shape: the country has been unwritten. They find a survivor, the cartographer Ilsa Marrow, who once sold guild secrets. Emotional beat: fear tempered by the first sparks of reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She confesses her old betrayal — she drew the maps the enemy used — and reveals the Door of Anew lies beyond the Ashfall Reach, three days' travel through terrain that rewrites itself nightly. Xanthe must decide whether to trust her. Emotional beat: bitter reckoning; forgiveness offered grudgingly, not yet earned.

chapters.title: Ashfall Reach
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The journey begins. Falling ash spells out words in dead languages; the party shelters in a chapel where prayers are answered by nothing. Xanthe and Wren share a watch, and something unspoken finally gets spoken. Emotional beat: tenderness discovered mid-catastrophe, guilt about wanting a future when there may be none.

chapters.title: What the Oath Costs
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ambushed by hollow soldiers made of erased names, Ilsa is gravely wounded buying the others time. Dying, she tells Xanthe the truth: the Door doesn't open for oaths kept — it opens for oaths broken and remade. Xanthe realizes their lifelong vow is the lock, not the key. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into terrible clarity.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The entity that unwrote the country — the Auditor, a faceless bureaucracy given hunger — summons them, offering restoration if Xanthe surrenders the guild ledgers and their sword. It shows Wren what they are: a leftover scrap of the unwritten, given flesh. Emotional beat: seduction of despair; identity itself held hostage.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe breaks their original oath aloud, feeling it tear free like a tooth, and attacks the Auditor to buy escape. Wren chooses to stand with them, claiming a name of their own making. They flee toward the Door as the country begins collapsing inward. Emotional beat: liberation and terror entwined — freedom costs everything they were.

chapters.title: The Door of Anew
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At the threshold, the Door demands a new oath in blood. Xanthe speaks one binding themselves to Wren and the survivors, not to any guild or crown — and holds the Door against the Auditor's final surge while everyone passes through. Emotional beat: climax; love enacted as sacrifice, identity chosen rather than assigned.

chapters.title: Maps We Draw Ourselves
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the far side, refugees camp under strange, living stars. Xanthe, oathless and unbound, opens a new ledger — not of debts, but of names worth keeping. Wren begins drawing the map of wherever they'll go next. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; belonging rebuilt from choice, grief carried gently forward.
